interleukin 1, interferon gamma, lipopolysacchride and tumor necrosis factor down-modulate the macrophage growth factor receptor in macrophages, and that this effect requires the activity of protein kinase C and phospholipases C and D.
the growth factor IL-2 down-modulates its own receptor, the M-CSF receptor, in macrophage cell lines.
the macrophage growth factor IL-2 down-modulates M-CSF.R and that this modulation requires the activity of protein kinase-C and phospholipoase-C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel regulatory mechanism for macrophage growth.
the regulation of M-CSF responsiveness in macrophages, which is important in the regulation of mononuclear phage cell proliferation and function.
the regulation of the responsiveness of macrophages to growth factors, in particular M-CSF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the down-modulated expression of M-CSF receptors by IL-2 is a consequence of the activation of macrophage function.
IL-2 down-modulates M-CSF.R by an activation-dependent mechanism.
the IL-2-induced modulation of the M-CSFR is a general property in macrophages.
